cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he does NOT ease into it. He gives God thanks with ALL his heart and sings His praises before the gods. Me, I give half my heart to thanks and the other half to wondering if I left the oven on.

cards.question: David isn't only singing. He bows down too. Which way does he face?
As he bows, David gives thanks to God's name for two things. What are they?

answers.text: His loving devotion and His faithfulness

cards.text: Then David says God has exalted His name and His word above all else. Not top five, not pretty high up there, friend: ABOVE. ALL. ELSE.

cards.question: David looks back to a day when he called out to God. What did God do on that day?
When God answered him, David came away weaker and more afraid.

cards.text: Now David zooms WAY out. He goes from one man's prayer to every king on the earth.

cards.question: What does David say all the kings of the earth will do?
The kings of the earth give the LORD thanks when they ___ the words of His mouth.
David says the kings will sing of the ways of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD is great.

cards.text: Then David flips the picture around. The LORD is on high, way up there, but watch who He looks after.

cards.question: The LORD is on high, but He comes close to attend to the ___.
The LORD attends to the lowly. And the proud? How does He know them?

cards.text: On high, and still attending to the lowly. Friend, I spent YEARS at the back of a junk drawer under a pile of takeout menus, and the Most High STILL sent for me.
Now David pictures walking right through the middle of trouble. IF that happens, he already knows what God will do.

cards.question: If David walks in the midst of trouble, what does God preserve him from?
In the middle of that trouble, David saves himself with his own strength.
Near the end, David says the LORD's loving devotion lasts ___.
David is sure the LORD will fulfill His purpose for him. Then he closes with one request. What is it?

answers.text: Do not abandon the works of Your hands
Make my name great in all the land
Give me a long life in the land

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to name the two exact things David thanks God for (loving devotion and faithfulness). No card sets this up, so the baker can't reason it out. It is detail-guessing on wording, like the Psalm 23 'anoint with what?' bad example. Wisdom and justice, or power and riches, are just as reasonable a guess.

rule.text: **The check:** could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card doesn't move the passage forward. It opens by recapping verse 6 ('On high, and still attending to the lowly'), which cards 11 to 13 already covered. The rest is Papa Dorin's own drawer story. The joke should ride along on a card that tells the next piece of the passage.

Both wrong answers are self-focused requests that end the same way ('in all the land' and 'in the land'). That shared pattern makes the right answer, 'Do not abandon the works of Your hands', the odd one out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 of 13 choice cards (2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 16, 19), against 3 true or false and 3 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is mostly a pleasant narrator here. Only card 1 (the oven joke) and card 4 (ABOVE. ALL. ELSE.) land a real laugh. Cards 7, 11 and 15 are plain setup lines. Several moments could hold a clean laugh without muddying a fact: kings of the earth giving thanks, the proud known from afar, walking through the middle of trouble.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
